clue.text: Not working is unacceptable

definitions.meaning: first meaning: broken, as of a machine
second meaning: improper, beyond what is allowed

explanation.surface: Someone declares that skiving off simply will not do.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one sentence about idleness; it is two separate meanings of the same phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes a broken machine and also behaviour that breaks the rules of decent conduct.

clue.text: Chilled portion of ham you left by top of fridge

indicators.note: a ham is a radio amateur, so this is a word as it is broadcast over the air

parts.note: a portion is a piece, and the word for calm sounds the same

indicators.note: the top of a word in a down clue is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of fridge
U is text-speak for you
L is the standard abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A slice of ham is left out for you on top of the fridge to keep cool.
explanation.walkthrough: PEACE, F, U and L make PEACEFUL; ham here is the radio amateur whose spoken word sounds like piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Chilled is slang for relaxed and calm, free of any stress or agitation.

clue.text: Concerning sex had when tense adult's held in wind

indicators.note: something held in another thing sits inside it, so these letters go within the other word

parts.note: to wind is to coil
A is the film-rating abbreviation for adult
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: A stressed grown-up struggles with flatulence during intimacy.
explanation.walkthrough: TA goes inside COIL after its I: COI-TA-L.
explanation.definitionFit: Coital describes coitus, the act of sexual intercourse that two people have had.

clue.text: Whistle-blower collaring vacuous pair's dog

indicators.note: collaring means seizing round the neck, so one word wraps around the other

parts.note: an informer is said to sing, so a whistle-blower is a singer

indicators.note: vacuous means empty, so the word loses its insides and only its outer letters stay

parts.note: the outside letters of pair

explanation.surface: A whistle-blower grabs a dog belonging to an empty-headed couple.
explanation.walkthrough: To sing is underworld slang for informing to the police, which is why a whistle-blower fits here.
explanation.definitionFit: A springer is a spaniel breed, so it is one kind of dog used for flushing game.

clue.text: Individual in street seen with reefer primarily?

definitions.text: Individual in street seen with reefer primarily?

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street
an individual is one

indicators.note: primarily means at first, so only the opening letter of the word before it is used

parts.note: the first letter of reefer

explanation.surface: A lone figure on the street is spotted with a joint.
explanation.walkthrough: ONE placed in ST, followed by R, makes STONER; read whole, the clue also describes one.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoner is a habitual cannabis smoker, the sort of person seen loitering with a reefer, slang for a joint.

clue.text: Supermodel is clingy type a Rolling Stone avoids

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Kate, the famous British supermodel

definitions.text: clingy type a Rolling Stone avoids
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the plant that clings to rocks, which a rolling stone gathers none of

explanation.surface: A supermodel is a clinging girlfriend whom a Rolling Stones rocker steers clear of.
explanation.walkthrough: Kate Moss dated rock stars, which suits the surface; the proverb is 'a rolling stone gathers no moss'.
explanation.definitionFit: Kate Moss is a famous supermodel, and moss is the low plant that grows clinging to stones and banks.

clue.text: An example would be smoke signal seen over reservation originally

indicators.note: a word seen over another covers it, so it spreads around the other letter

parts.note: a cue is a signal to act

indicators.note: originally means at the start, so only the first letter of the word before it is used

parts.note: the first letter of reservation

explanation.surface: Smoke signals are spotted rising over a Native American reservation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smoke' and 'signal' look like one phrase but smoke belongs to the definition; R goes inside CUE.
explanation.definitionFit: Smoking meat or fish preserves it, so smoking is one method of curing food.

clue.text: Can I cop out after buggering up job?

indicators.note: something buggered up has been messed about, so the preceding letters come out jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A worker who has made a mess of things asks whether they may quit.
explanation.definitionFit: An occupation is the work by which someone earns a living, the same as a job.

clue.text: Plump US man captured in draughts in Twister?

parts.note: plump means chubby
Americans call draughts checkers, and each piece there is a checker

explanation.surface: A fat American is caught in a cold breeze inside a tornado.
explanation.walkthrough: Draughts suggests cold air and Twister a tornado, but both are games here; in draughts the pieces are called men.
explanation.definitionFit: Chubby Checker was the American singer whose 1960 hit The Twist made him the dance's best-known performer.

clue.text: Work involved in diplomacy repelled Trump, perhaps

indicators.note: something involved in a thing is wrapped up inside it
something repelled is driven back, so the word is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: tact is diplomacy
OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Tactful negotiations were rebuffed by the American president.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the diplomacy word is turned round; the work goes into it afterwards, splitting off its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A top cat is the boss or person in charge, and the president is the top dog of the nation.

clue.text: One who might organise sex with topless duke

indicators.note: topless means without the top, so the word loses its first letter

parts.note: sexual union is a coupling
dukes is slang for fists

explanation.surface: Someone arranges a liaison with a half-naked aristocrat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put up your dukes' means raise your fists, so a duke is a FIST; without its top it is IST.
explanation.definitionFit: A trade unionist organises fellow workers into a union to bargain collectively with employers.

clue.text: Group of swingers whip contrary, line-crossing noob

indicators.note: contrary means going the opposite way, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: to whip is to flog

indicators.note: the line is crossed by the other word, which straddles it on both sides

parts.note: a cub is a novice, as is a noob
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A newcomer awkwardly blunders into a kinky wife-swapping party.
explanation.walkthrough: Swingers suggests partner-swapping, but these are golfers swinging clubs.
explanation.definitionFit: A golf club is an association whose members all swing at golf balls, hence a group of swingers.

clue.text: Band or group of Le Pétomane, say, out of France

parts.note: G stands for group, as in the G7

indicators.note: out of means leaving, so the letter for the country departs from the word

parts.note: Le Pétomane was a French music-hall performer famous for flatulence
F is the international vehicle code for France

explanation.surface: A query about a music band associated with France's famous wind-breaking entertainer.
explanation.walkthrough: Band looks like a musical group, which 'or group' seems to confirm, but it is the definition alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A garter is an elastic band worn round the leg to hold up a stocking.

clue.text: Cleric not dancing? Drug needed first is E!

indicators.note: needed first places the drug at the front of the rest

parts.note: E is slang for ecstasy

indicators.note: dancing letters move about and end up in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A priest who will not hit the dance floor learns that ecstasy is the prerequisite.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the single letter at the end, as in e-mail or e-book.
explanation.definitionFit: The prefix E abbreviates electronic, as in e-commerce, so the letter itself stands for the word.

clue.text: Her peccadillo aroused a Greek know-it-all

indicators.note: aroused means stirred up, so these letters are stirred into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A woman's little sexual indiscretion excited a smug Greek.
explanation.definitionFit: The oracle at Delphi was the ancient Greek priestess consulted because she supposedly knew everything, past and future.

clue.text: Lackey of orange crackpot seen in Houston on vacation

indicators.note: seen in places these letters within the city's remaining letters
on vacation the city is emptied out, so only its outer letters remain

parts.note: the first and last letters of Houston

indicators.note: crackpot means crazy, so the letters go mad and rearrange

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A toady of the orange-faced lunatic is spotted in Texas on holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Orange crackpot' reads as a jibe at a certain politician; orange is the anagram fodder and crackpot its signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A hanger-on is a sycophantic follower who attaches themselves to someone powerful, much like a lackey or servile attendant.

clue.text: Yours truly is an example of one making PM recoil

definitions.text: Yours truly is an example of one

indicators.note: making suggests building something new out of raw material, so these letters are reworked

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The writer boasts of being the sort who makes the Prime Minister flinch.
explanation.walkthrough: Yours truly is the setter, Hoskins, speaking about themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: A crossword setter is often called a compiler, since they assemble the grid and clues.

clue.text: Old soldiers mostly out of it in a state

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for old
the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
someone out of it, drunk or stoned, is gone

explanation.surface: Elderly veterans are largely wasted and in a bad way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a state' looks like a phrase meaning upset, but 'a state' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Oregon is one of the fifty United States, on the Pacific coast north of California.

clue.text: Vessel in WC upended? Went out without relief in the end!

indicators.note: upended means turned upside down, which in a down entry flips the word

parts.note: a bog is British slang for a toilet

indicators.note: without means lacking, so that letter is taken away

parts.note: went out means left

indicators.note: in the end points to the final letter of the word before it

parts.note: the last letter of relief

explanation.surface: Someone overturned a toilet and stormed off still desperate.
explanation.walkthrough: BOG flips to GOB, and LEFT loses its F to give LET; vessel is a drinking cup here, not a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A goblet is a drinking vessel, a stemmed cup with a bowl for wine.

clue.text: Reckon Hoskins must open unopened premium Bud

indicators.note: to open something is to split it apart and get inside
unopened means without its opening, so the first letter goes

parts.note: premium goods are the best
bud, short for buddy, is a mate
the setter, Hoskins, refers to themselves as I

explanation.surface: The setter reckons he must crack open a cold, quality bottle of Budweiser.
explanation.walkthrough: Bud looks like the beer brand; it is short for buddy. Setters often call themselves I or me.
explanation.definitionFit: To estimate is to reckon, roughly calculating or judging a figure.

clue.text: Group sat around could be The Sensations!

indicators.note: around suggests the letters being moved round into a new arrangement

parts.note: a set is a group
taken as written

explanation.surface: A band hanging around might be the soul group called The Sensations.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sensations reads as a band name, but it is plain sensations.
explanation.definitionFit: Tastes are sensations of flavour perceived by the tongue.

clue.text: Ball that one might wish a player would receive?

definitions.text: Ball that one might wish a player would receive?

parts.words: Ball that one might wish a player would receive?
parts.note: surface reading: a wish of good fortune for an actor, broken limb and all
setter's reading: a cricket delivery spun from the leg side towards the off

explanation.walkthrough: Actors are told to break a leg for luck, so the wished-for thing is a broken leg; in cricket the phrase names a spinning delivery.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a leg break is a ball spun by the bowler so it turns from the batter's leg side to off.

clue.text: Test screening of kiss by West gets sent up

indicators.note: sent up in a down entry means read from bottom to top
screening means hiding behind, so the name surrounds the kiss

parts.note: Mae West, the Hollywood actress
X is the kiss at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: A film screening of a kissing scene with Mae West is mocked.
explanation.walkthrough: X goes inside MAE, then the whole is reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: An exam is a test of knowledge, short for examination.

clue.text: Romeo pursing hearts, you might say, and love?

definitions.text: Romeo pursing hearts, you might say, and love?

indicators.note: pursing, read as pursuing, puts the lover's letter after the others, chasing them

parts.note: hearts is an example of a suit in cards
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O
Romeo is R in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's Romeo chases after affection and love.
explanation.walkthrough: SUIT and O come first, with R chasing behind; the whole clue also describes a wooer.
explanation.definitionFit: A suitor is a man courting a woman, and Romeo is the archetypal lover pursuing someone's heart.

clue.text: Crapulent carouser outside church in Newmarket?

indicators.note: outside means around, so the jumbled letters enclose the church
crapulent means drunk and unwell, so the following letters stagger about

parts.note: taken as written
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A drunken reveller sprawls outside a church in a Suffolk town.
explanation.walkthrough: Newmarket, a town in Suffolk, is the home of British horse racing; the question mark flags it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Newmarket is a famous English venue for horse racing, so it is an example of such a track.

clue.text: Turn performing in front of an audience in Wicked

indicators.note: to turn the word round is to read it backwards

parts.words: performing in front of an audience
parts.note: a live show is performed before an audience

explanation.surface: An act performs on stage in the musical Wicked.
explanation.walkthrough: Turn looks like a stage act, and Wicked like the musical; turn is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Evil means morally bad or sinful, the same as wicked.
